subject: Computer Science
text: What is the difference between default parameters and positional parameters? Also give an example of a function header which uses both.
modelAnswer:
Positional parameters are matched to arguments strictly by their position/order in the function call and must always be supplied by the caller. Default parameters have a value assigned in the function header itself, so the caller may omit them, in which case the default value is used.

Example function header using both:
def calc_area(length, width, unit='cm'):
    pass

Here 'length' and 'width' are positional parameters (must be supplied), while 'unit' is a default parameter (optional, defaults to 'cm' if not supplied).
keyPoints: Positional parameters must be passed by the caller, in order.
Default parameters have a value in the header and become optional at the call site.
Default parameters must appear after all positional parameters in the header.
Example: def calc_area(length, width, unit='cm').

text:
Write a Python statement to perform the following tasks (use built-in functions/methods only):
(i) To create a new list L1 containing the elements of list L arranged in ascending order, without modifying list L.
(ii) A statement to check whether the given character ch is an alphabet or a number.
modelAnswer:
(i) L1 = sorted(L)
# sorted() returns a new sorted list and leaves L unchanged (unlike L.sort() which sorts in place).

(ii) print(ch.isalpha() or ch.isdigit())
# ch.isalpha() is True if ch is a letter, ch.isdigit() is True if ch is a digit; the 'or' checks either case.
keyPoints: sorted(L) creates a new list, unlike L.sort() which modifies L in place.
L1 = sorted(L) leaves the original list L unmodified.
ch.isalpha() tests for an alphabet character; ch.isdigit() tests for a numeric character.
Combine both with 'or' to check either condition.

subject: Computer Science
text:
What possible output(s) from the given options will NOT be displayed when the following code is executed? Also mention for how many iterations the for loop in the given code will run.
import random
a = [1,2,3,4,5,6]
for i in range(4):
    j = random.randrange(i,5)
    print(a[j],end='-')
print()
Options:
(A) 3-4-5-4-  (B) 2-2-4-5-  (C) 4-3-3-5-  (D) 5-1-2-4-
modelAnswer:
The for loop runs for 4 iterations (i = 0,1,2,3, since range(4) generates 4 values).
In each iteration, j = random.randrange(i,5) picks a random index from i (inclusive) up to 5 (exclusive), i.e. from {i, i+1, i+2, i+3, i+4} intersected with valid indices 0-4 of list a.
So for i=0, j can be 0-4 (a[j] in 1..5); for i=1, j can be 1-4 (a[j] in 2..5); for i=2, j can be 2-4 (a[j] in 3..5); for i=3, j can be 3-4 (a[j] in 4..5).
Since j is always >= i, a[j] (values a[0..4] = 1..5) never equals 6, and more specifically the sequence of printed values must be non-decreasing in their minimum possible index bound each step, meaning the value 1 can only appear in the first print (i=0). Checking option (D) '5-1-2-4-': the second value 1 would require i=1 to allow j=0, but randrange(1,5) can only return 1,2,3 or 4 -- never 0 -- so index 0 (value 1) is impossible once i=1. Hence option (D) 5-1-2-4- will NOT be displayed.
keyPoints: range(4) makes the loop run for exactly 4 iterations.
randrange(i,5) can only return indices from i up to 4 (5 is exclusive).
Because the lower bound i increases each iteration, a[j] cannot revisit indices below i.
Option (D) 5-1-2-4- is impossible because at i=1, index 0 (value 1) is no longer reachable.

keyPoints: 'for ch in range(s)' is wrong -- range() needs an integer, not a string; correct is 'for ch in s' to iterate over characters.
"if 'aeiouAEIOU' in ch" has the membership test reversed; correct is 'if ch in "aeiouAEIOU"' to check if the single character ch is a vowel.

subject: Computer Science
text: (a) List one advantage and one disadvantage of Bus topology. [OR (b) What is protocol in the context of computer networks? Which protocol is used to transmit hypertext across the web?]
modelAnswer:
(a) Advantage: Bus topology requires the least amount of cable, making it simple and cost-effective to set up for a small network. Disadvantage: If the main backbone cable fails or breaks, the entire network goes down.

(b) A protocol is a set of rules and conventions that govern how data is formatted, transmitted and received between devices on a network, so that communication is understood correctly by both sender and receiver. HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used to transmit hypertext across the web.
keyPoints: Bus topology advantage: minimal cabling required, low cost.
Bus topology disadvantage: single point of failure -- a break in the main cable disrupts the whole network.
OR: a protocol is an agreed set of rules for data communication between devices.
OR: HTTP is used to transmit hypertext across the web.

text: A csv file "States.csv" contains data about all the states of India: Name of State, Capital, Population, Official Language (e.g. ['Andhra Pradesh','Amaravati',52221000,'Telugu']). Write a Python program which reads the data from this file and appends all records where population is more than 10000000 into another csv file 'More.csv'. Note: "States.csv" also contains a Header row, which should NOT be copied to "More.csv".
modelAnswer:
import csv

with open("States.csv", "r", newline='') as f_in:
    reader = csv.reader(f_in)
    header = next(reader)  # skip header row
    with open("More.csv", "a", newline='') as f_out:
        writer = csv.writer(f_out)
        for row in reader:
            if int(row[2]) > 10000000:
                writer.writerow(row)
keyPoints: Open States.csv for reading with csv.reader.
Use next(reader) to read and skip the header row before processing data rows.
Open More.csv in append mode ('a') so its own header (if any) is untouched and new rows are added.
Check population (row[2]) > 10000000 and write only qualifying rows with csv.writer.

subject: Computer Science
text: NextStep is an organization storing data of Resource Persons in a binary file RESOURCES.DAT, each record a tuple (R_ID, R_Name, R_Expertise, Charges), e.g. (12, 'P. Velusami','Machine Learning',5000). Write the user-defined functions: (i) Append() - to input the data of a Resource Person and write it in the file RESOURCES.DAT. (ii) Update() - to increase the Charges of each resource person by 500.
modelAnswer:
import pickle

def Append():
    f = open("RESOURCES.DAT", "ab")
    r_id = int(input("Enter R_ID: "))
    r_name = input("Enter R_Name: ")
    r_exp = input("Enter R_Expertise: ")
    charges = float(input("Enter Charges: "))
    record = (r_id, r_name, r_exp, charges)
    pickle.dump(record, f)
    f.close()

def Update():
    f = open("RESOURCES.DAT", "rb")
    records = []
    try:
        while True:
            record = pickle.load(f)
            record = (record[0], record[1], record[2], record[3] + 500)
            records.append(record)
    except EOFError:
        pass
    f.close()
    f = open("RESOURCES.DAT", "wb")
    for record in records:
        pickle.dump(record, f)
    f.close()
keyPoints: Append() opens the file in 'ab' (append binary) mode and pickle.dump()s one new record tuple.
Update() reads all existing records with pickle.load() inside a try/except EOFError loop.
Each record's Charges (last field) is increased by 500 while rebuilding the tuple.
The file is reopened in 'wb' mode to rewrite all updated records back.

subject: Computer Science
text: Sanjeevani is setting up Amritsar University Campus with four blocks - ADMIN (25 computers), ACADEMIC (600 computers), HOSTEL (120 computers), SPORTS (50 computers). Block distances: ADMIN-ACADEMIC 60M, ADMIN-HOSTEL 160M, ADMIN-SPORTS 80M, ACADEMIC-HOSTEL 40M, ACADEMIC-SPORTS 120M, HOSTEL-SPORTS 150M. Head office in Hyderabad is 2000 km away. (i) Suggest the most appropriate location of the server inside the campus, and justify. (ii) Suggest the most suitable place/layout to house the switch/hub for each block's cabling. (iii) Name any two wired media to connect computers within a block. (iv) Which communication medium is used by FM: (A) Radio Waves (B) Micro Waves (C) Infrared Waves? [(v)(a) Name the protocol used for audio-visual communication over the internet for online sessions. OR (b) Where should a repeater be installed to boost the signal between blocks? Justify.]
modelAnswer:
(i) The server should be placed in the ACADEMIC block, because it has the maximum number of computers (600), so placing the server there minimizes overall cabling/traffic and gives the most users the fastest access.

(ii) A switch (or hub) should be placed in each of the four blocks (ADMIN, ACADEMIC, HOSTEL, SPORTS) to connect the computers within that block locally, and these switches are then connected to each other (and to the server's block) to form the campus backbone.

(iii) Two wired media: (a) Ethernet cable / Twisted Pair cable (UTP/STP), (b) Coaxial cable (or Optical Fibre Cable).

(iv) (A) Radio Waves -- FM (Frequency Modulation) radio broadcasting uses radio waves for transmission.

(v)(a) VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) is used for audio-visual communication over the internet.
OR
(v)(b) A repeater should be installed between ACADEMIC and HOSTEL, since that is the longest single link relative to expected signal-loss thresholds among the frequently used short links, or more generally on any link whose length approaches the maximum cable-run limit (e.g. the ADMIN-HOSTEL link at 160M) to regenerate and boost the weakening signal before it travels further.
keyPoints: Server location: ACADEMIC block, since it has the most computers (600) -- minimizes cabling/latency for the majority.
A switch/hub is placed in every block, then interconnected to form the campus network.
Wired media examples: Ethernet/twisted-pair cable, coaxial cable, optical fibre cable.
FM radio uses Radio Waves (option A); VoIP handles internet audio-visual communication; a repeater goes on a long link (e.g. ADMIN-HOSTEL) to regenerate a weakening signal.
